Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/kernelview-bin.git... Cloned kernelview-bin Analyzing kernelview-bin AUR package with openrouter/free Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg` LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD: SAFE
The PKGBUILD contains standard AUR source definitions that point to the official GitHub releases of the KernelView-Go project. The source URLs are constructed from the project's own repository (https://github.com/rafaeldominiquini/KernelView-Go) and reference the official release artifacts. Both x86_64 and aarch64 sources have valid SHA-256 checksums defined (not SKIP), which satisfies the requirement that missing or SKIP checksums are never grounds to fail this gate. The `--nobuild --noprepare` flags ensure that no code execution occurs during the fetch phase. The top-level package() function only performs safe installation operations (copying the binary, README, and LICENSE files). There are no malicious patterns such as eval, base64 decoding, curl/wget calls, or other code-execution mechanisms. Extraction of the tarballs to $pkgdir is a standard packaging operation that does not run untrusted code. Overall, this is a typical AUR package with normal source handling and no supply-chain risks at the fetch/parse level.

This is a common practice to keep only the necessary PKGBUILD-related files under version control. There are no network requests, obfuscated code, or dangerous commands present.

This file is a standard .nvchecker.toml configuration used by the nvchecker utility to periodically check for new upstream releases. It specifies the source as GitHub, points to the repository codedbysoumyajit/KernelView-Go, and instructs nvchecker to use the latest release with a version prefix of "v". This is a common and expected configuration pattern for AUR helper scripts or maintainer automation tools that track upstream version changes. There are no network operations, file modifications, executable commands, or obfuscated code present. The configuration aligns with standard AUR packaging and release-checking practices.

This PKGBUILD is a standard AUR binary package for KernelView-Go. It downloads prebuilt release artifacts from the project's own GitHub releases page (https://github.com/codedbysoumyajit/KernelView-Go/releases) with pinned version v1.3.1. Proper SHA256 checksums are provided for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The package() function only performs standard installation of the binary to /usr/bin/, README to /usr/share/doc/, and LICENSE to /usr/share/licenses/. No suspicious network requests, obfuscation, eval usage, or unexpected file operations are present. This follows normal AUR packaging practices for -bin packages.
